title: Micro-SLO Composition and Platform Consolidation Patterns
author: Evan Brooks
body:
Summary:
This document describes a practical set of patterns for composing micro‑SLOs across platform services and consolidating platform responsibilities to improve operational clarity, reduce alert noise, and align operator actions with tenant economic signals. It combines architectural guidance, dashboard and alert recommendations, operational runbooks, a short retrospective of a pilot, and next‑step roadmap items.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to platform services owned by the eng-platform team (allocators, prefetch coordinator, runtime routing, telemetry pipeline).
- Goal: give operators deterministic decision surfaces during degradation and make cost/latency tradeoffs explicit to product owners.
- Not in scope: customer application SLOs or model quality SLOs (handled by product/Applied ML).

Primary outcomes:
- A composable micro‑SLO taxonomy and examples
- Dashboard primitives and alert thresholds tuned for consolidation operational flows
- A runbook for graceful consolidation and operator playbooks for safe rollback
- Retrospective lessons from a Q4 2025 pilot and a prioritized roadmap for adoption

Owner and contributors:
- Owner: Evan Brooks (eng-platform)
- Contributors: Priya Nandakumar (SRE), Marco Li (runtime), Ana Gomez (observability)

Micro‑SLO taxonomy and composition rules:
1) Unit micro‑SLOs (low-level):
   - e.g., allocator.cpu_saturation_p50 < 65% (30s window), connection_pool.utilization_p95 < 80%
   - Action: local throttling or transient evictions; no global customer notifications.
2) Composite micro‑SLOs (service-level):
   - Example: tenant_token_latency_p95_across_runtime <= 250ms AND tenant_throughput_success_rate >= 99.5%
   - Action: trigger consolidation workflow (see runbook).
3) Business impact SLOs (customer-facing):
   - e.g., api_text_generation_p99_latency < 1s or api_error_rate < 0.5%
   - Action: customer incident, public comms, and dedicated rollback.

Composition rules (operationally enforced):
- Prefer conjunctive composition for safety (A AND B) except when cost control requires disjunctions for graceful degradation.
- Tag each micro‑SLO with: service, steward, default remediation action, and cost impact estimate (tokens/sec-equivalent).
- Maintain a "composability matrix" (see table below) to enumerate safe and unsafe combinations.

Config table: micro‑SLO metadata (example rows)
| key | steward | window | threshold | remediation | cost_impact_estimate |
| allocator.cpu_saturation_p50 | eng-platform/allocator | 30s | 65% | soft_eviction | 8 tokens/sec |
| runtime.kv_cache_miss_p95 | eng-serving-runtime | 60s | 12% | increase_prefetch | 14 tokens/sec |
| telemetry.ingest_lag_p90 | eng-platform/telemetry | 2m | 90s | backpressure_routing | 2 tokens/sec |

Dashboards and visual primitives:
- Canonical dashboard layout (one per composed SLO):
  1) Top row: composed SLO status (red/yellow/green), current burn rate, and owner card.
  2) Middle row: contributing micro‑SLO panels with heatmap (trend over 6h, 24h, 7d).
  3) Bottom row: economic signal — token cost delta, estimated spend impact, and active consolidation credits.
- Visual primitives to create: sparkline + current_value + slow_change_indicator (small delta arrow).
- Shared short query snippets (to be copied into dashboards):
  - "composed_slo_status(service, window)" -> boolean rollup of tagged micro‑SLOs
  - "economic_delta(tenant, interval)" -> token-equivalent cost delta estimator

Alert design and thresholds (examples):
- Severity: P0 (immediate ops interrupt), P1 (operator action within 15m), P2 (investigate in next oncall shift).
- Sample rules:
  - P1: composed_slo_burn_rate >= 1.2 for 5m AND composite_error_rate > 0.3% -> page on‑call SRE.
  - P2: single micro_slo breach lasting 15m but composite still green -> ticket for steward, no page.
- Noise reduction strategies:
  - Only page when composed SLO trips or when two or more independent micro‑SLOs breach within a 10m window.
  - Suppress lower severity alerts when platform consolidation workflow is actively running.

Consolidation workflow (operator runbook) — rapid reference:
1) Detection:
   - Observe composed SLO flagged on dashboard or receive P1 page.
2) Triage (first 5 minutes):
   - Identify which micro‑SLOs are breached and their stewards.
   - Run the diagnostic script: /ops/bin/compose-diagnose --slo <id> --since 10m (returns ranked causes).
   - Check economic delta panel and active burst credits.
3) Immediate mitigations (5–20 minutes):
   - If allocator.cpu_saturation_p50 high: enable soft_eviction for non-critical tenants (soft_eviction policy id: se-policy-3).
   - If runtime.kv_cache_miss spikes: enable cohort_prefetch for high-hit cohorts for 10 minutes.
   - If telemetry.ingest_lag high: switch to reduced-sampling ingest mode and route backpressure to low-cost region.
4) Consolidation decision (20–40 minutes):
   - If mitigations recover composed SLO to green: schedule followup postmortem and mark actions in ticket.
   - If not recovered: escalate to consolidation plan B (regional burst shift with explicit tenant credits) and notify product owners.
5) Rollback and monitoring (40+ minutes):
   - Roll back experimental mitigations in reverse order if they cause regressions.
   - Keep composite dashboard pinned for 2h and monitor economic delta for cost spikes.

Runbook checklist (operator copyable):
1) Page received: confirm paging context.
2) Attach composed SLO link to incident ticket.
3) Run compose-diagnose and capture top 3 suggested causes.
4) Execute immediate mitigation(s) with rollback plan.
5) Update ticket with times and actions, set follow-up postmortem.

Safe consolidation patterns (architectural guidance):
- Consolidate routing and prefetch decisions under a single coordinator service to avoid split-brain in mitigation.
- Maintain an immutable mapping of "consolidation credits" per tenant to authorize temporary resource moves.
- Implement feature toggles for consolidation mitigations with built-in guard rails (max-duration, cost-threshold).

Pilot retrospective (Q4 2025):
What we did:
- Ran a two-week pilot consolidating three micro‑SLOs (allocator CPU, runtime cache miss, telemetry ingest lag) into a single composed SLO for a low-latency tenant cohort.
Outcomes:
- Alert volume for the cohort dropped 43% (fewer transient pages).
- Mean time to mitigation decreased by 26% because operators had a single decision surface.
- However, cost spikes occurred during an automated cohort-prefetch mitigation on two occasions (root cause: missing cost_impact_estimate tagging).
Action items from pilot:
- Require cost_impact_estimate for every micro‑SLO (blocked mitigations with unknown cost).
- Add a cost-safety limiter to prefetch mitigations (max token-equivalent per minute).
- Expand composed SLO dashboards and default suppressions to reduce page storms.

Metrics we measured:
- Alert volume, MTTR, cost delta, composed_slo_recovery_rate, false_positive_pages.
- Baseline -> pilot improvements available in the attached experiment sheet (see related_pages).

Roadmap (next 6 months):
- M1 (30 days): Publish composability matrix and annotate existing micro‑SLOs with cost_impact_estimate.
- M2 (60 days): Implement compose-diagnose CLI and two canonical composed SLO dashboards.
- M3 (90 days): Add cost-safety limiter to prefetch and soft_eviction mitigations.
- M4 (120+ days): Expand to regional consolidation patterns and run a second pilot across multiple regions.

Operational responsibilities and RACI (short):
- R: eng-platform (compose orchestration, dashboards), eng-serving-runtime (runtime micro‑SLOs), eng-sre (oncall/runbooks).
- A: eng-platform lead.
- C: product owners for affected tenants.
- I: finance and customer success for cost/customer-impact communication.

Templates and links (copy to incident ticket):
- Composed SLO ticket stub: [Composed SLO incident template]
- Dashboard links: [Composed SLO dashboard template 1], [Economic delta panel template]
- Diagnostic CLI: /ops/bin/compose-diagnose (internal tool)

Follow‑ups and governance:
- Quarterly audit: each composed SLO must have a documented steward, cost estimate, and a signed acceptance from product owner.
- Monthly retros: eng-platform runs a 30-minute retrospective on consolidation incidents and updates playbooks.

- Toggle soft_eviction: /ops/bin/evict-toggle --policy se-policy-3 --enable --duration 10m --reason "composed_slo_mitigation"
